name: Administrator account script execution
summary:
**Conversation Overview**

The person was working to install and run Claude Code on an older Windows machine, starting with a PowerShell execution policy error blocking npm scripts. Claude walked them through setting the execution policy via `Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser`, which resolved that issue. Claude Code then failed to launch due to the system running Windows PowerShell 5.x rather than PowerShell 7, so Claude guided them through installing PowerShell 7 via `winget install Microsoft.PowerShell`. The person noted the machine was an older Dell running Windows 11, and the winget install took approximately 40 minutes due to hardware constraints.

The person mentioned being behind on payments and unable to run Claude Code, pivoting to needing help downloading Albion Online game files manually. They had uploaded a `manifest.xml` file from the Albion Online autoupdate system. Claude parsed the manifest, and the person provided both the CDN base URL (`https://live.albiononline.com/autoupdate/`) and their local install directory (`C:\Program Files (x86)\AlbionOnline\game\Albion-Online_Data`). Claude built a parallel PowerShell download script using `System.Net.WebClient` background jobs with size-based file verification and resume capability. After the person requested progress visibility, Claude added a live-refreshing progress bar with percentage and MB counters. A parsing error on line 53 (`$name:` being misread as a drive reference) was fixed by switching message delimiters from `:` to `|`. Claude also provided the full list of all CDN URLs from the manifest covering win32, macOS, Linux, Android, iOS builds, patches, and launchers. The person prefers pastable inline code blocks rather than file deliverables, and wants scripts to include progress feedback.

chat_messages.text:
Classic execution policy block. Run this in your current PS window (you're already in system32 as admin, so it'll take):

```powershell
Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser
```

Then retry your npm install. `RemoteSigned` allows local scripts to run freely and requires downloaded scripts to be signed — it's the standard dev workstation setting and won't break anything.

If you want it machine-wide instead of just your user scope, swap `-Scope CurrentUser` for `-Scope LocalMachine`, but user scope is sufficient for npm to work.

You already have PowerShell — it's just detecting the old Windows PowerShell (5.x) instead of PowerShell 7. Two options:

**Quickest fix — install PowerShell 7:**
```powershell
winget install Microsoft.PowerShell
```
Then relaunch and run `claude` again.

**Alternative — if you have Git for Windows already installed**, find your bash.exe (usually `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe`) and set the env variable:
```powershell
$env:CLAUDE_CODE_GIT_BASH_PATH = "C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe"
claude
```

Do you have Git for Windows installed already?
